subtitleNullable: Registered UAV RGB-thermal wildfire pairs: smoke, fire, person
descriptionNullable:
# RGBT-3M — UAV RGB + Thermal Wildfire Dataset

Registered RGB and thermal image pairs captured by drone over outdoor wildfire
scenes, annotated for **smoke, fire and person**.

Mirror of the dataset released with *A UAV-Based Multi-Scenario RGB-Thermal
Dataset and Fusion Model for Enhanced Forest Fire Detection*
(Remote Sensing 2025, 17(15), 2593) — https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/17/15/2593
Re-uploaded here for convenience; the original is distributed via Quark Netdisk,
which requires a Chinese phone number to access.

## Provenance

- **Authors:** Yalin Zhang, Xue Rui, Weiguo Song et al., State Key Laboratory of
  Fire Science, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)
- **Original host:** https://complex.ustc.edu.cn
- **Capture hardware:** DJI M300 RTK + Zenmuse H20T, and DJI Mavic 2 Enterprise
- **Locations:** Anhui, Yunnan and Inner Mongolia, China
- **Registration:** RGB/thermal pairs aligned with the authors' M-RIFT method
- **Annotation tool:** LabelImg

Please cite the paper above if you use this data.

## Structure

RGBT/
├── rgb/{train,test}/ visible-spectrum frames (640x480, 3-channel)
├── thermal/{train,test}/ thermal frames (640x480, grayscale in RGB container)
├── labels/{train,test}/ YOLO-format boxes
└── data.yaml
`rgb/` and `thermal/` use **identical filenames** — that's how pairs are linked.
Both modalities share **one** label set, since the pairs are registered.

11,220 pairs: 7,854 train / 3,366 test (70/30).

## Classes and instances

| id | class | instances | median box area (% of frame) | ≈ px at 640x480 |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | smoke | 13,574 | 5.12 | ~125 x 125 |
| 1 | fire | 11,315 | 0.195 | ~24 x 24 |
| 2 | person | 5,888 | 0.231 | ~27 x 27 |

30,777 instances total. Note the **26x scale gap** between smoke and fire —
smoke is large and diffuse, fire is small and sharp. The 10th percentile of
fire boxes is ~0.03% of frame (roughly 10 x 10 px), so this is a genuine
small-object detection problem.

## Caveats

- **Bounding boxes only — no segmentation masks.** LabelImg produces boxes.
- **No negatives.** All 11,220 frames contain annotations. The paper describes a
  further 6,642 non-fire pairs; they are not in this release. False-positive
  rate therefore cannot be measured on this data alone — pair it with a
  hard-negative set for that.
- **Smoke in thermal.** One label set covers both modalities, but the paper
  notes their thermal sensor could not resolve smoke at range, so class 0 may
  not be meaningfully visible in `thermal/`. Verify before training a thermal
  smoke detector.
- **Directory naming.** The original archive used `images/` (RGB) and `image/`
  (thermal) — one character apart. Renamed here to `rgb/` and `thermal/`. If you
  use Ultralytics' default label discovery (which rewrites `/images/` to
  `/labels/`), you will need to pass label paths explicitly or add an `images/`
  symlink.
- Ultralytics `.cache` files and per-split `classes.txt` were removed; the caches
  contained absolute paths from the original author's machine.

## License

Released by the original authors for research purposes. Cite the paper.
